articles.targetQuestionText: Light of wavelength λ gives a stopping potential of 3V₀. Light of wavelength 2λ gives V₀ for the same metal. What is the metal’s threshold wavelength?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q42; question ID 69112142; PDF page 17

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q32; question ID 695278257; PDF page 11
pyqs.independentSolution: φ=hν0, so the lowest threshold frequency gives the smallest work function and largest Kmax for equal incident photon energy.

articles.title: How much of a first-order reaction is finished?
articles.learningObjective: Distinguish fraction remaining from fraction reacted, and explain why two half-lives do not complete an ideal first-order reaction.
articles.example: 100 units of R become 50, 25 and 12.5 units after successive half-lives.
articles.targetQuestionText: For a first-order reaction R → P, what fraction of the original reactant has reacted after time t, if the rate constant is k?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q57; question ID 695278282; PDF page 20
pyqs.independentSolution: Initial fraction 1; remaining exp(-kt); reacted 1-exp(-kt). At t=0 answer=0; at one half-life answer=1/2.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q58; question ID 69112158; PDF page 23
pyqs.answer: Zero order: twice the initial half-life. First order: no finite exact completion time in the ideal model.
pyqs.independentSolution: Zero order R=R0-kt gives t_complete=R0/k=2 t_half. First order R=R0 exp(-kt) stays positive at finite t.

review.notes: The original Q58 option prints an awkward power-of-half-life notation for infinite completion. articles.title: When are capacitors in series or parallel?
articles.learningObjective: Identify common-potential connections before combining capacitors; distinguish shared voltage from successive voltage drops.
articles.example: The four-capacitor PYQ circuit is redrawn using the same three connection points A, X and B.
articles.targetQuestionText: In the circuit above, C₁ = C₂ = C₃ = 1 μF and C₄ = 2 μF. What is the equivalent capacitance between A and B?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 2; Q37; question ID 695278412; PDF page 14
pyqs.independentSolution: C1 and C2 share A and X, so give 2 μF in parallel. This is in series with C4=2 μF, giving 1 μF. C3=1 μF is directly between A and B, so total=2 μF. Nodal cross-check at VA=1,VB=0 gives VX=1/2 and QA=2 μC.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q32; question ID 69112132; PDF page 12–13
pyqs.independentSolution: The dielectric fills half the gap across the full area, not half the plate area. Each half thickness d/2: air 2C, dielectric 10C; successive voltage drops give 1/Cnew=1/(2C)+1/(10C), hence 5C/3. Increase=2/3=66.67%.

review.notes: Original wire routing visually inspected. C1 and C2 are not in series despite their positions in a row. Dielectric problem explicitly uses half the gap and neglects edge effects; introduction to dielectric capacitance is required before this extension. articles.title: Why does osmotic pressure depend on particle count?
articles.learningObjective: Compare osmotic pressure using dissolved-particle concentration i times molarity, and preserve concentration when mixing equal-concentration solutions.
articles.example: Two equal-volume solutions separated by a membrane that passes water but retains all dissolved ions.
articles.targetQuestionText: At 27 °C, a membrane separates 1 L of 0.1 M K₄[Fe(CN)₆] on side x from 1 L of 0.1 M FeCl₃ on side y. Only water can cross. Assuming complete dissociation, which side is hypotonic?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 2; Q54; question ID 695278429; PDF page 20–21
pyqs.answer: Side y (FeCl₃) is hypotonic relative to side x.
pyqs.independentSolution: Complete dissociation gives K4[Fe(CN)6] ->4K+ +[Fe(CN)6]4- (5 particles) and FeCl3 -> Fe3+ +3Cl- (4). At equal T, effective concentrations are 0.5 and 0.4 mol/L. Side y has lower osmotic pressure. Initially water flows y to x at equal external pressure.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 2; Q55; question ID 691121205; PDF page 21–22
pyqs.answer: All three osmotic pressures are 9.96 × 10⁻⁴ bar.
pyqs.independentSolution: Protein A: (1/50000)/0.5=4e-5 mol/L. B: (2/50000)/1=4e-5. Mixture: (3/50000)/1.5=4e-5. Pi=cRT=4e-5*0.083*300=0.000996 bar. Dilute solution volumes approximate stated water volumes; additive volumes and non-dissociating protein are the ideal question model.

review.notes: Original MCQ is paraphrased as the keyed hypotonic-side question. The complex ion stays intact; no claims about colour mixing across the water-only membrane. articles.title: How can sums of squares give standard deviation?
articles.learningObjective: Recover the sum and sum of squares from shifted-square totals, then calculate variance and standard deviation using divisor n.
articles.example: The numbers 2, 4 and 6, then the same three numbers shifted by 5, show that spread is measured about the mean.
articles.targetQuestionText: For ten numbers x₁, x₂, …, x₁₀, the sum of all (xᵢ + 2)² is 180 and the sum of all (xᵢ − 1)² is 90. What is their standard deviation?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 2; Q8; question ID 695278383; PDF page 3–4
pyqs.independentSolution: Let S=sum x and T=sum x². T+4S+40=180 and T-2S+10=90. Subtraction:6S+30=90, S=10. T=100. Mean=1, variance=100/10-1=9, standard deviation=3.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 2; Q9; question ID 691121159; PDF page 4
pyqs.independentSolution: Last value is 8n-48. Sum squares is n(16+64)=80n. Thus496+(8n-48)²=80n, giving 4n²-53n+175=0=(n-7)(4n-25). n must be an integer; n=7 and last value=8. Remaining six can satisfy sums48,496 (mean8, variance56/3), so the root is feasible.

review.notes: Use n, not n−1, for the descriptive variance in these JEE questions. Distinguish sum of squares from square of sum; the constant term in each shifted square occurs ten times. The second quadratic root 25/4 is inadmissible.
